automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector
collector_scope: Raw-only public-source collection for AI-assisted development practice updates. No docs/wiki pages or raw/processed files were updated.

cutoff_window.date_rule: Include only sources with a direct visible publication or update date within the last 2 days relative to the run timestamp. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

federation_boundary.local_scope: Practice-level implications for AI-assisted development workflows, governance, verification, context, adoption, permissions, and operating model.
federation_boundary.handling_rule: For upstream-owned entities, record the entity as upstream-owned and keep only the downstream practice implication or routing note.

qualifying_updates.title: Private evals become the deployment gate for coding agents
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AI Cost Check used Real-SWE as a prompt to describe production readiness as a private, ticket-based eval loop. The guide recommends representative historical tickets, CI-equivalent test harnesses, review gates, cost logging, results warehousing, and model routing by task difficulty rather than global benchmark rank.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The update directly supports wiki coverage that agent approval should be scoped to task classes and repository evidence, with self-critique treated as iteration rather than a final approval gate.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local guidance should frame private evals around mergeable PR rate, test evidence, reviewer rubric, permissions, failure reasons, and cost per resolved task for each approved model-task pair.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route broad benchmark, model, and tool catalog details upstream; retain the private eval architecture and approval-boundary pattern locally.

qualifying_updates.title: Harness-level context engineering addresses long agent runs
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: MarkTechPost summarized context engineering as a harness responsibility for long-horizon agent work, citing context overflow, goal loss, and missing state as predictable failure modes when tasks span many tool calls. The article points to harness mechanisms rather than model swaps as the layer that keeps work coherent.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The article gives a practice-level bridge between context architecture and agent harness design: durable state, summaries, task decomposition, and goal tracking are operating controls for coding agents.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local pages can treat context engineering as harness behavior: maintaining task state, externalizing memory, constraining goal drift, and preserving decision history across long runs.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Do not create a broad AWS or harness product page locally; ingest only the reusable practice pattern if used.

qualifying_updates.title: Claude Code debate separates throwaway prototypes from reviewable production code
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Business Insider reported on Boris Cherny's response to a developer worried about AI-generated code quality. The discussion contrasted reviewable AI-assisted production code, where the submitting developer can explain and maintain changes, with low-blast-radius throwaway prototypes that may be treated more like black boxes.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The item is useful practice evidence for separating code-quality obligations by blast radius, expected lifetime, and maintainability rather than adopting a single rule for all AI-generated code.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local coverage can describe a production-readiness rule: AI-assisted production changes remain explainable, reviewable, and maintainable by an accountable developer, while disposable prototypes may use lighter review if the blast radius is low.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route individual biography and product background upstream; keep only the code-quality operating distinction locally.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent sandbox risk shifts from model behavior to surrounding tools
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Origami summarized three recent disclosures in which coding agents or their surrounding tooling could execute attacker-controlled content from project files or sandbox outputs. The article highlights Git core.fsmonitor execution, tool allowlist gaps, Docker socket exposure, editor task settings, and delayed patching across CLI coding agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The analysis is directly relevant to agent permission practice because it treats opening an unfamiliar repository with an agent as an execution event, not just a read event.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local governance guidance should cover external-code intake, inventorying agent versions, keeping production credentials off developer machines, using isolated first-open environments, and centralizing deployment paths with limited permissions.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Security vulnerability details may belong in the upstream security wiki; local ingestion should focus on AI-assisted development workflow controls.

qualifying_updates.title: Real-SWE cost analysis ties review gates to model-specific failure modes
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Daily Brief analyzed Specific Labs' Real-SWE benchmark and emphasized cost per resolved task and model-specific failure patterns. The article argues that engineering teams should choose coding agents by working-change economics and design review gates around the failure modes of the agent and harness they actually deploy.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This source complements private-eval coverage by connecting eval results to review-gate design, model routing, and renewal economics rather than treating benchmark rank as the primary decision.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local eval pages can distinguish leaderboard discovery from deployment proof and require review gates that are tailored to known failure modes for the chosen agent stack.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: If ingested with the AI Cost Check item, de-duplicate shared Real-SWE background and preserve only the additional cost/review-gate angle.

qualifying_updates.title: AI vendor review questions shift from SOC 2 to prompt supply chain evidence
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Daily Brief argued that AI vendor security review should ask who processes prompts, whether no-training terms apply to the actual tier, maximum retention including flagged content, what voids indemnity, whether the deployed feature is tested, and whether the feature is in certification scope. It compares major platform terms as of September 12, 2026.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The article gives concrete review questions for teams adopting AI assistants, coding agents, API tools, and retrieval apps where prompts may cross provider or subprocessor boundaries.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local governance pages can turn these into a durable intake checklist for AI-assisted development tools: data processors, retention ceilings, no-training contract scope, feature-specific assurance, and certification boundaries.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Preserve vendor-specific details as source-attributed evidence; avoid local broad platform encyclopedia coverage.

qualifying_updates.title: Local CLI coding agents framed as a privileged-laptop risk
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Podcast Summary recapped a Latent Space discussion in which Quinn Slack argued that local CLI coding agents inherit developer laptop permissions, including shell credentials, keys, local history, and authenticated internal services. The suggested alternative is remote disposable sandboxes with short-lived, narrow OIDC tokens and monitored execution.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The source gives practice-level evidence for evaluating where agents run, how credentials are scoped, and whether audit logs exist for shell commands and token exchanges.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local guidance should compare local agent execution against cloud sandbox execution using blast radius, credential inheritance, temporary access, monitoring, and reproducibility as decision criteria.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use cautiously as a podcast summary; verify against the original episode before treating claims as primary evidence.

qualifying_updates.title: Mandatory code review challenged by parallel agent workflows
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Podcast Summary recapped Quinn Slack's argument that mandatory pre-merge human review can erase the parallelism gains from AI coding agents. The summary describes a shift from mean-time-between-failure thinking toward fast recovery, automated rollback, trusted ownership, and selective review based on service criticality.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The item captures an emerging operating-model tension: teams need review gates, but the shape of the gate may differ for low-risk internal tools versus critical production systems.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local source-workflow guidance can record the decision axis: mandatory review, automated tests, rollback speed, ownership, and risk-tiering should be tuned together rather than copied wholesale from pre-agent development norms.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use as a candidate discussion source, not a blanket recommendation; any durable wiki synthesis should preserve risk-tier boundaries.
